newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria plans to sell stake in Expressbank.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria plans to sell stake in Expressbank.

text.p: Bulgaria plans to sell a majority stake in the Varna-based Expressbank early next year as part of its delayed bank stabilisation programme, a Bank Consolidation Company (BCC) official said on Tuesday.

"We are prepared to start negotiations this month or at the begining of next year with a serious investor from whom we have received an offer for buying a big stake in Expressbank," BCC executive director Valentin Tzvetanov told Reuters.
The BCC manages state equity in local commercial banks.
Local media recently reported that Austria's Raiffeisenbank Bulgaria was interested in acquiring a majority stake in Expressbank.
"The BCC would not insist on retaining a blocking vote and may cut state equity below 25-30 percent depending on agreements reached with the investors," Tzvetanov said.
The Italian Banca Agricola Mantovana acquired a five percent stake in Expressbank last month, which after a capital increase approved by Expressbank shareholders on Tuesday is reduced to 1.2 percent.
A shareholders' extraordinary meeting raised the share capital to 3.57 billion levs from the current 713 million levs.
So far the state through the BCC holds more than 96 percent of Expressbank's share capital and the remainder is distributed among private investors.
"BCC's contribution is estimated at 2.851 billion levs and was covered with domestic bad loan bonds worth $15 million," a bank official said.

Expressbank and the United Bulgarian Bank were the only state-owned financial institutions where private investors subscribed to part of the new share issues after the banks were recapitalised with state support.
In June the cabinet distributed $400 million bad loan bonds issued by the government among seven state-owned banks in a bid to boost their capital to risks assets ratio.
